title: Numerical Computation Engine — Overview and definition
t: Numerical Computation Engine — Overview and definition
description: Executes large-scale numerical algorithms — linear algebra, quadrature, ODEs, and optimization — with controlled error.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Executes large-scale numerical algorithms — linear algebra, quadrature, ODEs, and optimization — with controlled error. A numerical computation engine provides dense and sparse linear algebra (BLAS/LAPACK-style), numerical quadrature, interpolation, root finding, and eigensolvers with documented error bounds. Real implementations include NumPy/SciPy, Julia's standard library, Eigen, and GSL. The engine tracks floating-point error, condition numbers, and convergence, and reports when a result is unreliable.
capabilities: Dense and sparse matrix factorizations (LU, QR, Cholesky, SVD)
Adaptive quadrature and multidimensional integration
Nonlinear root finding and least-squares fitting
Eigensolvers for symmetric and nonsymmetric problems
Error estimates, condition numbers, and convergence diagnostics on every solve

description: Executes large-scale numerical algorithms — linear algebra, quadrature, ODEs, and optimization — with controlled error.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. How Numerical Computation Engine is actually implemented. A numerical computation engine provides dense and sparse linear algebra (BLAS/LAPACK-style), numerical quadrature, interpolation, root finding, and eigensolvers with documented error bounds. Real implementations combine C/Fortran ABI (BLAS/LAPACK), Python API (NumPy/SciPy), Julia API, CLI for batch jobs with An optimized BLAS (OpenBLAS/MKL), LAPACK, a threading runtime. The implementation is verified by Verify against the NIST Statistical Reference Datasets and LAPACK test matrices: residuals must sit below documented tolerances and certified values must match to the stated digits

title: Numerical Computation Engine — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Executes large-scale numerical algorithms — linear algebra, quadrature, ODEs, and optimization — with controlled error.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Numerical Computation Engine, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Dense and sparse matrix factorizations (LU, QR, Cholesky, SVD)). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Dense and sparse matrix factorizations (LU, QR, Cholesky, SVD) and Adaptive quadrature and multidimensional integration. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Matrix and linear algebra solver) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
